allow.@base-ui-components/react: House stack. Unstyled, accessible primitives so this library owns appearance and not keyboard or ARIA behavior. Pinned to the 1.0 RC line.
allow.next: House stack. Framework for the local development and documentation site, and the RSC boundaries this library must honor.
allow.@vanilla-extract/css: Styling layer. Zero-runtime CSS from TypeScript, so design tokens are typed and a style file is safe to import from a server component.
allow.@vanilla-extract/rollup-plugin: The vendor-supported way to compile .css.ts during a library build. Emits real CSS next to each module instead of leaving .css.ts for consumers to compile.
allow.rollup: Library bundler. Needed over tsc alone because .css.ts files have to be compiled, not type-stripped, and preserveModules keeps one output file per source file so client boundaries and tree-shaking survive.
allow.@rollup/plugin-node-resolve: Lets Rollup resolve the bare specifiers that vanilla-extract emits while every runtime dependency stays external.
allow.vitest: Test runner. Shares the Vite transform pipeline, so .css.ts files load in tests the same way they build.
allow.jsdom: DOM for component tests. Needed to render and assert on a component's states.
allow.@testing-library/react: Queries components through the accessibility tree, which is how the state and focus requirements in design.md get asserted rather than assumed.
allow.eslint: Lint. react-hooks rules are enforced on every edit, so the config has to exist.
allow.typescript-eslint: Type-aware lint rules. Pinned to the 8.x line because it does not yet accept TypeScript 7.
allow.eslint-plugin-react-hooks: Supplies the react-hooks rules the harness blocks on.
allow.prettier: One formatter, so a public repo has no formatting noise in its history.
allow.globals: Environment global lists for the ESLint flat config. Avoids hand-maintaining browser and node global names.
allow.mixpanel-browser: Analytics. Sam reads this product in Mixpanel already, and the SDK is what carries device and session identity; a hand-rolled POST to the HTTP API would report every visit as a new person. Apache-2.0. If it goes away, lib/analytics is the only importer and the site runs without it: no token, no calls, nothing else changes.
allow.@types/mixpanel-browser: Types for mixpanel-browser, which ships none of its own.
